subject: Archaeology
title: Ceramic Analysis: Stories in Pots
description: A quick win: understand Ceramic Analysis: Stories in Pots.

hook.text: Pottery is the most common find on most archaeological sites — and one of the most informative.

buildup.text: Clay composition reveals where a pot was made. Decoration and shape reveal when and by whom it was crafted.

discovery.text: Chemical analysis can match a pot to a specific clay source, proving trade routes that stretched hundreds of miles.

twist.text: Residue analysis detects what was inside. Traces of wine, olive oil, and even chocolate have been found.

climax.text: The oldest known chocolate was found inside a 3,900-year-old pot in Mesoamerica — 1,500 years before the Maya.

punchline.text: A broken pot is never just a broken pot. The clay, the shape — everything speaks.

quiz.question: What can residue analysis of ancient pottery reveal?
options: The exact recipe used to make the pot's clay
What was stored inside — wine, oil, milk, and even chocolate
The temperature at which the kiln was fired
